grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Ich, du, er/sie/es, wir, ihr, sie, and the polite Sie. Sie (capital S) is formal and works for one or many people.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Plurals are irregular. Learn each noun with its plural. The plural article is always "die". Common endings: -e, -en, -er, umlaut, -s, or no change.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: Take off -en, then add: -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en. Example: machen (to do).

grammar.title: Gehen: to go
text: Going to do something soon: use gehen or the future. Ich gehe schlafen = I am going to sleep.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb is always in position 2. Subject, verb, rest. If you start with time or place, the verb stays second, and the subject moves after it.
rows: with a second verb at the end

grammar.title: Negation
text: Use nicht (not) for verbs and adjectives. Use kein (no / not a) for nouns.
nicht negates verbs, adjectives and adverbs (ich arbeite nicht). kein negates a noun that has "ein" or no article (ich habe kein Auto). Also: nichts (nothing), niemand (nobody), nie (never).
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Yes or no question: put the verb first. With a question word: question word, then verb, then subject.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: du / dein / dir for friends. Sie / Ihr / Ihnen for strangers. With Sie, the verb is the same as "they" (sie ... -en).

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Spoken past: haben / sein + past participle (ge-...-t or ge-...-en). Future: werden + infinitive.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal (du): verb stem, no ending (komm!, geh!). Plural (ihr): -t (kommt!). Formal (Sie): infinitive + Sie (kommen Sie!). Negative: add nicht (komm nicht!).

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: können (can), müssen (must), wollen (want) + infinitive at the END: ich kann schwimmen, wir müssen gehen, ich will essen. nicht müssen = need not; nicht dürfen = must not.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: auf (on top of), unter (under), in (in), neben (next to), bei / in der Nähe von (near), um neun Uhr (at nine). Place words take the dative when you say where something is.
ex: the book is on the table
das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: adjective + er = comparative (groß, größer); am + adjective + sten = the most (am größten). als = than. gut, besser, am besten (good, better, best).

grammar.title: Everyday sentences
text: Extra practice with the most useful patterns.
ex: wir sind in den Park gegangen
veer zint in dayn park geh-GAHNG-en
